When you research an asset, only the asset symbol (e.g. NVDA) is sent to InvestED's serverless function to fetch market data.

All of this stays on your device and can be exported or deleted from the "Data Controls" page. No tracking or advertising cookies are used.
terms_p_1: InvestED is an educational platform for learning about investing. The service does not constitute investment advice, financial advice, tax advice, or a recommendation to take any action in securities.
terms_p_2: All content in the system — including risk scores, investor classifications, sample portfolios, and market data — is presented for educational and illustrative purposes only, and does not constitute a recommendation to take any action. Consult a licensed professional before making investment decisions.
terms_p_3: The system is provided for personal and educational use. Content may not be copied, reproduced, or distributed without attribution.
faq_a_1: No. InvestED is an educational platform only. It does not provide investment recommendations and does not tell users what to invest in. All content — including the broker comparison table — is intended to teach concepts and help with orientation, not to recommend.
faq_q_2: How does the system analyze my profile?
faq_a_2: The system identifies keywords and phrases in the text you wrote (age, goals, risk, time horizon, financial knowledge, interests) and calculates a risk score and investor classification using transparent rules. The Explainable AI card shows exactly which signals were identified.
faq_a_3: Analysis runs in your browser and is not sent to an InvestED server. Some items - such as language preference, learning progress, and analysis history (only with your consent) - are stored locally in your device's localStorage, and can be exported or deleted from the "Data Controls" page. There is no cloud account and no remote sync.
faq_q_4: Are the market data on the dashboard real?
faq_a_4: Yes — in the live production version, market data is fetched in real time from Yahoo Finance, through a dedicated server function. The symbols shown are selected based on the interests identified in your profile. If the service is unavailable (e.g., in local development), the system automatically falls back to simulated data so the dashboard always works.
faq_q_5: How does the personal learning track work?
faq_a_5: The track is tailored to the financial knowledge level you indicated. Beginners get a full track from the basics. Those who already understand the material get a shorter track that starts from the advanced stages, with the basics shown as optional refreshers.

about_general_desc: InvestED is a platform designed to teach investing in an interactive, transparent, and accessible way.
about_p1: InvestED is an independent FinTech product created, designed, and developed entirely by Saar Kessel — MBA and BA in Business Administration, with practical experience in the banking industry from two years at Bank Hapoalim, alongside a deep and ongoing interest in the world of investing, technology, and FinTech.
about_p2: This project is, to a large extent, my business card: it was born out of a clear perception that the investing world is full of terms and concepts that deter many people even to start learning about it, and out of a genuine desire to prove — not just tell — how to combine real financial knowledge with Full Stack development capabilities and advanced AI technologies, in order to turn a complex field into a simple, visual and interactive experience.
about_p3: Beyond the technical aspect, the project reflects an end-to-end Product Thinking approach: from defining the problem (accessibility of financial knowledge), through understanding the user and their needs, to selecting the technological architecture that supports it in the best way possible — exactly as expected from a real production product in a FinTech company.
quiz_q1_o1: A loan given to the government
quiz_q1_o2: A fund that holds a basket of assets and trades like a single stock
quiz_q1_o3: A type of bank savings account
quiz_q1_e: An ETF holds a basket of assets (stocks, bonds, etc.) and trades on the exchange like a stock — it's the simplest way to get immediate diversification.
quiz_q2: What is the main purpose of diversification?
quiz_q2_o2: To reduce risk by spreading across different assets
quiz_q2_e: Diversification is not meant to maximize profit, but to reduce risk — so that poor performance of a single asset won't sink the entire portfolio.
quiz_q3: What usually happens when someone tries to "time the market"?
quiz_q3_o1: It usually works only for professionals
quiz_q3_o2: It's very difficult to consistently predict peaks and troughs, even for experts
quiz_q3_o3: It's the safest way to invest
quiz_q3_e: Many studies show that even professional investors have great difficulty timing the market consistently — time in the market usually beats timing the market.
quiz_q4_o2: Earning returns on returns that have already been earned in the past
quiz_q4_o3: A fee charged by the bank on investments
quiz_q4_e: Compound interest is the engine behind long-term wealth building — money that earns returns, which themselves earn additional returns over time.
quiz_q5: What does a high volatility score represent?
quiz_q5_o1: The asset always goes up in value
quiz_q5_o2: The asset price moves significantly, both up and down
quiz_q5_o3: The asset is safer than average
quiz_q5_e: High volatility means large price movements in both directions — not just risk of decline, but also potential for sharp rises.
quiz_q6: What is a good example of a common beginner investment mistake?
quiz_q6_o1: Building an emergency fund before starting to invest
quiz_q6_o2: Consistent investing over time regardless of price (DCA)
quiz_q6_o3: Investing all savings in a single stock that received a "hot tip"
quiz_q6_e: Concentrating all savings in a single asset significantly increases specific risk — this is one of the most common mistakes made by beginning investors.
quiz_q7: What is the main difference between passive and active investing?
quiz_q7_o1: Passive tries to beat the market, active follows it
quiz_q7_o2: Active tries to beat the market, passive follows a low-cost index
quiz_q7_o3: There is no significant difference between them
quiz_q7_e: Active investing tries to select "better" assets than the market (usually at higher cost), while passive simply follows a broad index at low cost.

ai_insight_horizon_very_short: ⏳ Very short investment horizon. Over such a period, market volatility can have a significant impact on the outcome when the money may be needed.
ai_insight_horizon_medium_long: 📈 Medium-to-long horizon. Such a period allows compound returns and compound interest to become a significant factor in the outcome.

ai_insight_diversification_world: 🌎 The asset represents broader geographic diversification across markets. Such diversification may reduce dependence on a single market or geographic region.
ai_insight_diversification_sp500: 🇺🇸 The exposure is focused on large US companies. While there is variation between companies, there is still significant dependence on the performance of the US stock market.
ai_insight_diversification_nasdaq: 💻 The exposure is more focused on growth and technology companies. Such focus may increase growth potential, but also sensitivity to volatility and pricing changes.
ai_insight_diversification_bonds: 🛡️ Bonds tend to provide a more defensive character than a stock portfolio, but there are still risks such as interest rate changes, credit, and inflation.
ai_insight_diversification_cash: 💰 Cash provides high liquidity and low volatility, but over time there is exposure to inflation risk and the alternative cost of not investing the capital.
ai_insight_diversification_default: 🧩 The diversification level depends on the asset structure and additional assets in the portfolio. The system examines the asset as part of a broader picture, not as an isolated asset.
ai_insight_recommendation_very_short: ⚠️ In a very short horizon, significant weight should be given to liquidity and the ability to absorb a decline in value before the money is needed.
ai_insight_recommendation_short: ⚠️ In a relatively short horizon, it's important to examine whether the asset's volatility level is appropriate for when the money is expected to be needed.
ai_insight_recommendation_nasdaq: 📊 Due to the relative concentration in growth and technology companies, it's important to understand that the scenario may be more sensitive to market fluctuations. Diversification across assets can change the overall risk profile.
ai_insight_recommendation_sp500_long: 🚀 A long horizon can allow an investor to cope with volatility and take advantage of compound interest. However, actual returns are not guaranteed.
ai_insight_recommendation_world: 🌎 Broad geographic diversification can reduce dependence on a single region. However, this is still exposure to stock markets, so there is volatility.
ai_insight_recommendation_bonds: 🛡️ The bond character may be suitable for scenarios where relative stability is more important than maximizing growth potential, but bonds are not risk-free either.

quiz_q8: What is the main purpose of rebalancing a portfolio?
quiz_q8_o1: To sell everything when markets fall
quiz_q8_o3: To bring the allocation back to its target mix
quiz_q8_e: Rebalancing means periodically realigning the portfolio to its target allocation, which keeps risk at the intended level instead of drifting with market moves.
quiz_q9: Why does a low expense ratio matter over time?
quiz_q9_o1: Fees compound too, so small annual differences become large gaps
quiz_q9_e: An annual fee is charged every year on the whole balance, so even a 1% difference compounds into a very large gap over decades.
quiz_q10: What is a stock index like the S&P 500?
quiz_q10_o1: A basket that measures the performance of many companies together
quiz_q10_e: An index bundles many companies into one measure, letting investors follow the market as a whole instead of picking single stocks.
quiz_q11_o3: A rise in the general price level that erodes purchasing power
quiz_q11_e: Inflation means money buys less over time, which is why long-term savings need growth that at least keeps up with prices.
quiz_q12: What does liquidity mean for an investment?
quiz_q12_o3: How quickly and easily it can be converted to cash without a big loss
quiz_q12_e: Liquid assets can be sold quickly near their market price; illiquid assets may require time or a discount to sell.
quiz_q13: What usually happens to bond prices when interest rates rise?
quiz_q13_e: Existing bonds with lower fixed payments become less attractive when new bonds pay more, so their prices adjust downward.
quiz_q14: What is the relationship between risk and expected return?
quiz_q14_o1: Lower risk always means higher return
quiz_q14_o2: Higher expected return usually comes with higher risk
quiz_q14_e: Markets pay a premium for bearing uncertainty. A promise of high return with low risk is a classic warning sign.
quiz_q15: What is an emergency fund and why does it come before investing?
quiz_q15_o1: Cash covering several months of expenses so you never sell investments in a crisis
quiz_q15_o3: A fund that invests in emergencies
quiz_q15_e: An emergency fund prevents forced selling of investments at a bad time when unexpected expenses hit.
quiz_q16: What is the key difference between an ETF and a mutual fund?
quiz_q16_o2: ETFs trade on the exchange throughout the day like a stock
quiz_q16_e: Both pool investors' money, but ETFs trade continuously on the exchange while mutual fund units are priced once a day at NAV.
quiz_q17: Why can holding just one stock be risky even if the company is excellent?
quiz_q17_o1: It is illegal to hold one stock
quiz_q17_o2: Company-specific events can hit the whole investment at once
quiz_q17_e: Single-stock concentration exposes the whole portfolio to one company's specific risk, regardless of how good the company is.
quiz_q18: What does dollar-cost averaging (DCA) help with?
quiz_q18_o2: Reducing the impact of investing everything at a market peak
quiz_q18_e: Investing a fixed amount regularly buys more units when prices are low and fewer when high, smoothing the entry price over time.
quiz_q19_o1: The total debt of the company
quiz_q19_o2: Share price multiplied by the number of shares
quiz_q19_e: Market cap measures the equity-market size of a company, not its fair value or its profits.
quiz_q20: What does a high P/E ratio usually suggest?
quiz_q20_o2: Investors expect higher future growth, or the stock may be expensive
quiz_q20_e: A high P/E means investors pay more per unit of current earnings, usually reflecting growth expectations — or overpricing.
quiz_q21: What is the point of an investment horizon in planning?
quiz_q21_o3: It sets when you need the money, which shapes how much risk makes sense
quiz_q21_e: A long horizon allows riding out downturns; a short one calls for more stability because there is less time to recover.
quiz_q22_o3: A distribution of part of a company's profits to shareholders
quiz_q22_e: Dividends return part of the profit to owners, but they are never guaranteed and can be cut.
quiz_q23: What is NAV (net asset value) of a fund?
quiz_q23_o3: The fund's assets minus liabilities, divided by its units
quiz_q23_e: NAV is the per-unit value of what the fund actually holds; an ETF can trade slightly above or below it.
quiz_q24: Why does concentrating in one sector increase risk?
quiz_q24_o2: A shock to that sector hits the whole portfolio at once
quiz_q24_e: Sector shocks (regulation, demand shifts) hit all companies in the sector together, so concentration removes the protection of diversification.
quiz_q25: What is the main benefit of starting to invest early?
quiz_q25_o1: Markets only rise for young people
quiz_q25_o3: More time for compounding to work
quiz_q25_e: Compounding grows returns on returns, so each additional year multiplies the effect dramatically.

board_analyst_dividend: The 16% return includes the dividend of 2, not just the price move.
board_analyst_limits: Two invented years do not establish future returns, risk or valuation.
board_analyst_guarantee: The report guarantees another 16% return next year.
board_analyst_correction: The report cannot guarantee future returns. Remove that claim and cite the calculation plus its limits.
board_accountant_question: The chair asks: Cash rose 40. Does that mean the business is safely self-funding?
board_accountant_liquidity: Current assets of 900 / current liabilities of 600 = 1.5, but inventory is not cash.
board_accountant_funding: Operating 240 minus investing 300 leaves -60 before financing of 100.
board_accountant_limits: Debt terms, asset quality and future obligations need more evidence.

board_accountant_correction: The ratio does not prove solvency. Asset quality and payment timing still matter. Remove that claim.

game_personal_balanced_intro: I am Amir. My fictional loss tolerance is 7%. I want a balanced explanation of risk and opportunity.
game_personal_balanced_loss: We crossed my 7% loss tolerance. What evidence supports keeping this position?
game_personal_balanced_trust: I am losing confidence in the communication. Explain the trade-offs instead of guaranteeing a recovery.
game_personal_balanced_plan: How much of the portfolio is in one stock? Tell me what concentration means for my mandate.
game_personal_balanced_stayed: I stayed. Show me the final result after manager fees, not only the gross return.
game_personal_balanced_left: I left this fictional mandate after the recorded trust review. My decision is final for this run.
game_personal_growth_intro: I am Dana. I can accept up to 12% fictional loss, but growth is not permission to promise returns.
game_personal_growth_loss: Even my growth mandate has limits. The loss is beyond 12%; explain your next decision.
game_personal_growth_trust: I accept volatility, not poor communication. Tell me what is uncertain about this trade.
game_personal_growth_plan: What changed in the growth case today? Separate the fictional news from what we still do not know.
game_personal_growth_stayed: I stayed. Compare the final gain with the worst day-close drawdown before the next run.
game_personal_growth_left: I left despite my higher loss tolerance. Review my trust history, not just the final portfolio value.
desk_source_link: Selected report line. Bars use the same invented values as the table below. Each selection has its own scale.
desk_cash_bridge_note: Game units. Outflow left, inflow right; each half spans 300. Compare operating, investing and financing before your board decision.
game_scenario_note: Choose before the first order/reply. All instruments and scenario prices are fixed invented game inputs, not quotes, real funds or predictions. Charts reveal completed/current days only.
game_selected_exposure_note: Share of portfolio value in the selected fictional instrument. No yield, coupon, dividend or suitability model is included.
game_stress_news_0: Fictional stress desk: credit conditions tighten; no future prices are revealed.
game_stress_news_1: Fictional demand shock hits both stocks; the bond basket moves differently.
game_stress_news_2: Fictional refinancing concern pressures industry while growth partly rebounds.
game_stress_news_3: Fictional earnings warning: inspect concentration and client mandates.
game_stress_news_4: Fictional partial recovery; settlement is not a guarantee of profit.
game_client_plan_note: One commitment per client/day, separate from the reply. Cash-buffer: keep at least 25% cash at today’s close (+6 trust if met, -18 if broken). Monitoring: watch the day and report back (+4 trust when you explain today, -10 if you stay silent). No automatic trades or guaranteed protection.
game_plan_none: No risk plan committed for this day.
game_source_note: Inspect sourced prices separately from the fictional game. These prices do not execute orders, change the game ledger or affect clients. Data may be delayed, stale or unavailable.
game_source_coverage: Stocks, ETFs and mutual funds supported by Yahoo, not every listing. Enter the exact Yahoo symbol (e.g. AAPL, VTI, FXAIX or 0700.HK). Quotes and failures are cached for 15 minutes; no automatic polling.
game_source_unavailable: Source data unavailable. The API may be unavailable locally, rate-limited, or unable to resolve this symbol. No fictional price was substituted.
game_source_cached: Cached up to 15 minutes; historical data up to 6 hours.
game_candle_unavailable: Source OHLC is unavailable. No candles were invented from closing prices.
game_candle_guide: Green: close above open. Red: close below open. Wick: day’s high and low. O = open, H = high, L = low, C = close. Use the slider or point to a candle to inspect it.
practice_history_note: Self-reported practice on this device only, not verified work or a credential. Starting a new run keeps the last 20 completed summaries. Clearing browser data removes them.
practice_no_runs: Finish a run, then start another to keep its summary here.
practice_restart: Keep summary and start new practice
practice_restart_confirm: Keep this completed practice summary and start a blank practice run?
ops_title: Shared securities and mutual-fund back-office game
ops_disclaimer: Every transaction, cash value, custody record and NAV state in this case is invented. This is one shared educational operations desk, not real settlement, bank access, professional verification or current market rules. Source market prices are separate and never fix a case discrepancy.
ops_queue_note: Select a record. Compare both sides, read the control card and choose one action. Each choice saves locally.
ops_instruction: Check units, cash, reference and fund NAV. These records are fictional evidence, not a live bank or custodian feed.
ops_records_note: Case ledger comparison · invented game units
ops_duplicate: Reference already used: duplicate review required
ops_control_title: Control card: rules for this case only
ops_controls: Match only if units and cash agree, the reference is unique, and fund NAV is confirmed when applicable. Hold mismatches or pending NAV. Escalate duplicate references. Resolve each break with its supporting packet; multiple breaks need evidence for all of them. Rules in this card apply only to this case, not industry practice.
ops_retry: That action does not satisfy the case controls. Try again.
ops_reason_matched: Both books agree and the required valuation/reference checks pass. Matching is a review result, not a real payment instruction.
ops_reason_units: The position units differ. Hold and obtain corrected evidence; do not change one side just to make it match.
ops_reason_cash: Cash differs by 10 game units. Hold until the difference is explained.
ops_reason_nav: Fund NAV is pending. Matching quantities and cash alone cannot pass this control.
ops_reason_duplicate: REF-101 was already used by S-101. Escalate for review rather than matching a duplicate.
ops_closed: All six records were classified and resolved under the case controls. The review is locked locally. No real money moved or settlement was instructed. This is not a professional credential.
ops_conflict: This desk changed in another tab. Load the latest saved desk to continue.
ops_save_error: Could not save this case on the device. Your last saved record remains unchanged.
ops_glossary: NAV means the value of one fund unit. The custodian records positions; the bank record supplies cash evidence. Hold means stop the case workflow until evidence arrives, not sell the holding.
families_note: Choose a workflow, not a separate game for each job title. Shared tasks stay together; role-specific rules and source data remain separate. These are fictional educational exercises, not job credentials.
families_investment_task: Trade invented instruments, review risk and answer fictional clients.
families_research_task: Read an invented report, calculate results and defend evidence to a board.
families_reporting_task: Review invented statements, cash flow and a board conclusion.
families_operations_task: One queue, common reconciliation controls and fund-specific NAV checks.
ops_evidence_instruction: Classification alone is not closure. Select the evidence that supports this record, then record the fictional resolution.
ops_evidence_books: Both case books agree; reference is unique and any fund NAV is confirmed.
ops_evidence_position: Corrected custody statement: S-102 holds 5 units. Reference and cash unchanged.
ops_evidence_navApproval: Fund valuation approval: F-201 NAV confirmed for this case; 20 units and 1,000 cash agree.
ops_evidence_cashExplanation: Approved cash reconciliation: F-202 gross 500 less a separately documented fee of 10 equals bank net 490.
ops_evidence_duplicateReview: Duplicate-review decision: S-103 repeats REF-101. Cancel the duplicate record, keeping S-101.
ops_evidence_marketQuote: Use the current market price to make the case books agree.
ops_evidence_manualEdit: Change the bank/custody book without supporting evidence.
ops_evidence_rejected: That does not support this exception. A market quote is not a bank/custody correction, and an unsupported edit is not evidence.
ops_support_matched: Both sides already match; keep the reference and valuation evidence.
ops_support_units: The corrected custody evidence explains the missing unit.
ops_support_nav: This fund-specific valuation evidence clears the pending NAV control.
ops_support_cash: The documented fee explains the gross/net difference without pretending bank cash was 500.
ops_support_duplicate: The duplicate is cancelled, not processed twice or relabeled as matched.
ops_resolution_units: Resolved: custody correction recorded; original discrepancy remains visible above.
ops_resolution_nav: Resolved: fund valuation approval recorded; original pending state remains visible above.
ops_resolution_cash: Resolved: 10-unit fee documented; gross 500 and net 490 remain distinct.
ops_resolution_duplicate: Resolved: duplicate cancelled in this fictional review; original instruction preserved.
ops_resolution_note: Evidence packets and resolutions are invented teaching records. Original discrepancies remain visible for review. No real books are edited and no payment, settlement or cancellation is sent.
ops_legacy_closed: This earlier practice run was closed after classification under its original controls. It has no evidence-resolution record. Start a new run to practice the expanded workflow.
committee_title: More cases in this shared desk
committee_note: Short invented committee exercises, separate from the main game. Decisions save on this device; they do not certify professional judgment. Choose the action supported by the facts, not the most confident claim.
committee_conflict: These choices changed in another tab. Load the latest saved choices to continue.
committee_save_error: Could not save this choice on the device.
committee_facts_concentration: Invented portfolio: 80% in one stock, 20% cash. It gained 12%. The case review limit is 40% per issuer. A client asks to keep the allocation unchanged.
committee_reason_concentration: Targeted concentration review is required under this case limit. A gain does not cancel the breach. This is a fictional policy, not a market-wide rule.
committee_case_liquidity: Cash needed before a restricted holding can be sold
committee_facts_liquidity: Invented client needs 30 game units tomorrow. Cash is 10; the other 90 are in a holding that this case says cannot be sold for five days. There is no confirmed credit facility.
committee_reason_liquidity: Defer any claim that the cash need is covered. Liquid cash is 20 short; an unconfirmed facility and future sale proceeds are not evidence.
committee_facts_fundFees: Two invented funds report gross returns of 8% and 7.5%. Annual stated fees are 2% and 0.5%. Their risk, timing and fee methodology have not been compared. A pitch says the first fund is automatically better.
committee_reason_fundFees: Request a net-return and like-for-like risk review. Simply subtracting stated fees would suggest 6% versus 7%, but that rough exercise is not proof of comparable net performance or a recommendation.
committee_case_fundRisk: A fund with no current holdings evidence
committee_facts_fundRisk: An invented fund gained 15% last year. Its latest holdings, liquidity terms and exposure report are missing. The committee is asked to certify it as low risk today.
committee_reason_fundRisk: Defer the low-risk conclusion until the missing current evidence is available. Past return does not establish holdings or liquidity risk.
committee_facts_profitCash: Invented statement: profit 200, operating cash flow -50, receivables increased 250. The board proposes stating that profit means cash generation was strong.
committee_reason_profitCash: Request a receivables and cash-conversion review. Profit and operating cash are different measures; the given cash flow contradicts the proposed claim.
committee_case_funding: A positive cash balance with missing funding details
committee_facts_funding: Invented statement: operating cash 240, investment outflow 300, financing inflow 100. Cash rose 40. Debt maturity details are missing; the board asks to certify safe self-funding.
committee_reason_funding: Defer the safe self-funding claim. Operating cash minus investment is -60 before financing; a rise of 40 does not prove funding safety, and debt maturity evidence is missing.
committee_numbers_note: Invented case inputs. Compare the requested conclusion with both the numbers and the missing evidence.
committee_case_mandateFit: A documented fit to this case mandate
committee_facts_mandateFit: Invented mandate: at most 40% in one issuer and 20 game units available for the stated cash need. The proposal has 30% in the issuer and 25 liquid cash. No other check is required in this simplified case. The committee asks only whether these two controls pass.
committee_reason_mandateFit: Approve only the stated control check: 30% is below 40% and 25 covers 20. This does not promise returns, establish suitability or approve a real investment.
committee_facts_returnCalculation: Invented one-period share price rises from 50 to 56 and pays a dividend of 2. Assume no fees, tax or other cash flows for this calculation. The analyst reports a 16% total return and explicitly makes no forecast.
committee_reason_returnCalculation: Approve the narrow arithmetic claim: (56 - 50 + 2) / 50 = 16%. This is this fictional period’s total return, not next period’s return or a buy recommendation.
committee_case_cashBridge: A cash bridge with a bounded conclusion
committee_facts_cashBridge: Invented statement: operating cash 240, investment cash -300 and financing cash 100. The accountant reports a net cash increase of 40 and says this alone does not establish self-funding or solvency.
committee_reason_cashBridge: Approve that bounded statement: 240 - 300 + 100 = 40. The stated limitations prevent it being confused with funding safety or solvency.
ops_packet_numbers: Supporting packet values, not edits to the original books
committee_case_proposedWeight: A proposed trade crosses the case mandate
committee_facts_proposedWeight: A fictional portfolio has 35% exposure to one issuer. A proposed purchase would take it to 45%; the documented case mandate caps that issuer at 40%. The committee is asked to approve this purchase without changing the mandate. Current compliance alone does not show the proposed trade fits.
committee_reason_proposedWeight: Request a revised trade size. The proposed weight exceeds the case limit by 5 percentage points. Do not approve the purchase because the current 35% exposure is within the limit; no mandate change is supplied.
committee_case_dilutedEarnings: Basic earnings labeled as diluted earnings
committee_facts_dilutedEarnings: The fictional report gives net income of 120 game units, 60 weighted-average basic shares and 80 weighted-average diluted shares, with no other numerator adjustments. A memo claims diluted earnings per share are 2 game units. The committee is asked to approve that number.
committee_reason_dilutedEarnings: Request a corrected denominator and memo. Basic EPS is 120 / 60 = 2; diluted EPS in this case is 120 / 80 = 1.5. The reported 2 is not the supplied diluted calculation. This case does not model all accounting adjustments.
committee_case_accrualBridge: Revenue is reconciled without calling it cash
committee_facts_accrualBridge: An invented sales packet has booked revenue of 90 game units and collections of 30. Opening receivables are 0 and ending receivables are 60; the packet has no returns, taxes, write-offs or other movements. A memo states only that collections plus the increase in receivables reconcile to booked revenue. It does not call all revenue cash.
committee_reason_accrualBridge: Approve only the stated reconciliation: 30 + (60 - 0) = 90. Collections remain 30, not 90. This bounded calculation does not prove revenue-recognition compliance, audit quality or future collectability.
ops_reason_combined: Hold this case for both breaks: custody is one unit short and bank cash is 15 below the internal gross amount. Matching one field alone cannot clear the other discrepancy.
ops_evidence_combinedApproval: Combined approval packet: S-104 corrected custody is 6 units; documented fee is 15, reconciling gross cash 600 to net bank cash 585. Reference REF-104 remains unique.
ops_support_combined: The packet separately supports the missing custody unit and the 15-unit fee. Both original breaks remain visible above.
ops_resolution_combined: Resolved: corrected custody and the documented fee bridge are both recorded; original books remain unchanged.
game_client_plan_note_v1: One commitment per client/day, separate from the reply. Cash-buffer plan: keep at least 25% cash at today’s close (+6 trust if met, -18 if broken). Monitoring alone adds no trust. No automatic trades or guaranteed protection.
